thread.title: Getty group set for final gathering
thread.title_full: Getty group set for final gathering

author: ohtadmin
title: Getty group set for final gathering
text:
The ad hoc committee empaneled to assess Fort Getty and “ensure that this wonderful place continues to provide enjoyment” is expected to consider its final recommendations at 1 p.m. Tuesday, June 9.
“We recognize that no single set of recommendations will please everyone,” a draft of the report says. “The committee has sought opportunities to balance often divergent and competing interests, outlining a series of ambitious yet achievable steps to shape a park that residents can be proud of, enjoy, and share with others.”
The members — Marisa Quinn, John Potter, Casandra West, Bill Salmons and Richard Smith — have drafted a 15-point document of objectives, including five guiding principles that were “distilled from surveys, public input and decades of prior planning.”
“Without them, every future decision about the park risks reopening the same debates de novo, with no shared framework to guide or ground them,” the draft says. “While formally adopting these principles does not commit the town to a specific project or expenditure, it helps ensure that whatever this or future councils choose to do next will honor the community voice and ensure consistency. The committee’s recommendations were built on this foundation; the principles are the “why” behind every “what,” and adopting them first is what makes everything that follows coherent and defensible.”
The guiding principles include stewarding the park’s “distinctive character” by preserving its open, natural qualities while respecting its history. The next principles are “take pride in quality,” “be welcoming and neighborly” and “let revenue serve the park, not drive it.”
“Revenue is important and should fund improvement and stewardship, not shape the park’s character,” the report says. The final principle — “honor what residents value and serve all users” — says decisions should reflect the broad, diverse base of visitors rather than optimizing any single group.
The second objective is to clarify Fort Getty’s identity because a review of how Fort Getty is presented online “revealed inconsistent and somewhat inaccurate descriptions, sometimes emphasizing one characteristic over another,” the draft says. “Having clarity and consistency is essential to promote the park, manage expectations and limit confusion.”
The committee, which recommends the name “Fort Getty Park,” said the municipally owned 41- acre property is a public space for both residents and visitors. It is “valued for its water views, natural setting and shoreline access. Its range of features and uses make it one of the town’s most dynamic and visited public spaces, defined not only by what it offers, but by how people experience and use it.”
The third objective is to enhance the natural beauty of the park. “Nature preserve” ranked first among future priorities in the survey conducted by the committee with 84% of the 1,059 responses supporting that option.
The fourth objective is to expand opportunities for access. The committee emphasized improving batteries Tousard and Whiting while extending and linking the network of trails.
The fifth objective to renovate and expand bathrooms includes adding a facility near the boat ramp and providing at least one offseason facility.
The sixth, seventh and eighth objectives are related to camping. The recommendations include consolidating tent camping to the area near the gatehouse, reducing the RV park by 10 sites while adopting term limits and upgrading the electrical system to 50 amps.
The ninth objective is to “strengthen ongoing maintenance” and the 10th is to improve traffic flow and parking.
The 11th objective is to ensure accessibility and environmental sustainability are treated as crosscutting priorities, “woven into every capital project and program decision.”
The 12th objective is to engage “the Jamestown Historical Society in developing additional interpretive signage or programming to bring the park’s history to life.” The 13th would expand storage and the 14th would establish a standing advisory committee “charged with overseeing implementation, providing continuity between planning and execution, advising on policy questions as they arise, and reporting regularly to the council.”
The final objective is to “plan for the long term.” The committee’s approved recommendations will be forwarded to the town council for consideration.
summary: The ad hoc committee empaneled to assess Fort Getty and “ensure that this wonderful place continues to provide enjoyment” is expected to consider its final recommendations at 1 p.m. Tuesday, June 9.
